parts.label: (a)(i)
hints: Hint 1: Think about what power tells you about how fast energy is moved or transformed, rather than just how much energy there is.
parts.proper_answer: Power is the work done per unit time (rate of transfer of energy).
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What Power Really Means**
Power is all about speed of energy. Two machines can do the same amount of work, but the more powerful one does it faster. So you define it as how much work is done in each second.

Step 2: **Exact Definition**
In symbols, $$P = \frac{W}{t}$$ where $W$ is work done and $t$ is time taken. In words: work done per unit time.

parts.text: Use the definition of power to show that the SI base units of power are $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$.

markscheme_points.text: (P = W/t gives) units: kg m2 s-2 / s

hints: Hint 1: Start from $P = W/t$ and recall the SI base units already known for work done (energy): $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$. How does dividing by time change the powers of the units?
parts.proper_answer: Work has units $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$, so $P = W/t$ has units $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}/\text{s} = \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link Power to Work**
You know $$P = \frac{W}{t}$$ Work done $W$ is energy, and its SI base units are $$\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$$ Time $t$ has base unit $\text{s}$.

Step 2: **Divide the Units**
Put the units into the definition: $$\text{unit of } P = \frac{\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}}{\text{s}} = \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$$ That is exactly the required result.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The intensity $I$ of a sound wave moving through a gas is given by

$$I = f^2 A^2 v k$$

where $f$ is the frequency of the wave,
$A$ is the amplitude of the wave,
$v$ is the speed of the wave
and $k$ is a constant that depends on the gas.

Determine the SI base units of $k$.

markscheme_points.text: (I = P/A so) units of I: kg m2 s-3 / m2
units of f: s-1 and units of A: m and units of v: m s-1
units of k: kg s-3 / [(s-1)2 m2 m s-1] = kg m-3

hints: Hint 1: Recall that intensity $I$ means power per unit area. Use your result from (a)(ii) to work out the base units of $I$.
Hint 2: Write down the base units of each quantity on the right-hand side: frequency $f$ in $\text{s}^{-1}$, amplitude $A$ in $\text{m}$, and speed $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Hint 3: Rearrange $I = f^2 A^2 v k$ to make $k$ the subject, then substitute all the units and simplify the powers of $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$.
parts.proper_answer: $I$ has units $\text{kg s}^{-3}$. Rearranged, $k = I/(f^2 A^2 v)$ has units $\text{kg s}^{-3}/[(\text{s}^{-1})^2 \text{m}^2 \text{m s}^{-1}] = \text{kg m}^{-3}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Find the Units of Intensity**
Intensity is power arriving per unit area: $$I = \frac{P}{A_{area}}$$ Power has units $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$ from part (a) and area has units $\text{m}^2$. So $$\text{unit of } I = \frac{\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}}{\text{m}^2} = \text{kg s}^{-3}$$

Step 2: **List Units of f, A and v**
Frequency $f$ is number per second, so unit $\text{s}^{-1}$. Amplitude $A$ is a distance, so unit $\text{m}$. Speed $v$ is distance per time, so unit $\text{m s}^{-1}$. Therefore: $$\text{unit of } f^2 A^2 v = (\text{s}^{-1})^2 \times \text{m}^2 \times \text{m s}^{-1} = \text{m}^3 \text{s}^{-3}$$

Step 3: **Solve for the Units of k**
Rearrange the equation: $$k = \frac{I}{f^2 A^2 v}$$ Now put in the units: $$\text{unit of } k = \frac{\text{kg s}^{-3}}{\text{m}^3 \text{s}^{-3}} = \text{kg m}^{-3}$$ The $\text{s}^{-3}$ cancels, leaving density-type units. So the SI base units of $k$ are $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
